column4: Inside a small village pub in the evening: a low steady murmur of several men's voices talking quietly, words that cannot be made out, glasses clinking now and then, a chair scraping on wooden floorboards, a cough, a mug set down on a wooden table. No laughter, no shouting, no music. Seamless loop.
A small cheap plastic torch's thumb switch pushed forward: one crisp short mechanical click-clack, very close to the ear, dry, no room, no music, no voice.
A small cheap plastic torch's thumb switch pulled back off: one slightly softer, lower single click, very close to the ear, dry, no room, no music, no voice.

A small torch bulb shorting out in the hand: a sharp electrical crackle and fizz with a hard buzz, a tiny glass pop of the filament, then dead silence. Very close to the ear, dry, no room, no music, no voice.

Far away across a dark empty field at night, one man with his mouth shut hums a slow sing-song call of three notes, yuuu chuuu chuuu, high then low, stops, and calls it again exactly the same, nasal, wavering, not quite human, a long distant echo off a line of trees. No music, no wind.

A long way off in the dark someone is cheerfully calling a child home for supper, the words lost, only the friendly rising and falling tune of a man's voice through a closed mouth, muffled, the same phrase twice exactly the same, a faint echo over an empty field at night. No music, no wind.

Very far away at night a slow strange warbling call that could be a bird or could be a grown man imitating a bird badly with his throat, three rising notes, then a wet click, a silence, and again the same, thin and lonely in an open field, faint echo. No music, no wind.

A slowed down, pitched down, detuned old recording of a man humming a nursery tune with his mouth shut, heard from far outside through a wall, the melody bending flat at the end of each phrase, unnatural calm, distant, thin, no instruments, no music bed.
